This bail application is filed under section 482 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (for short 'BNSS').

2. Petitioners are accused Nos.1 to 3 in Crime No.431 of 2024 of Maradu Police Station, Ernakulam,
registered for the offences punishable under Sections 406, 419 and 420 r/w Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
3.

According to the prosecution, the accused had, with an intention to cheat the defacto complainant and her husband, entered into an agreement for sale of a property, having an extent of 71.80 Ares and after payment of an advance amount of Rs.78,00,000/- failed to pay the balance amount and induced the defacto complainant's husband to act as a guarantor and after obtaining the title deeds of the property by fraudulent means, kept the same as a security and thereby cheated the defacto complainant by not paying the balance purchase money and also created an encumbrance on the property.
4. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioners as well as the learned Public Prosecutor.

sentences.text: The issue raised in the FIR stems, from an agreement for sale between the defacto complainant and the 2nd accused.
Subsequently, after paying an advance amount, the defacto complainant's husband stood as a surety to the loan availed by the 3rd accused.
Considering the nature of allegations, it is noticed that the dispute primarily has the trappings of a civil dispute between the parties regarding an agreement for sale.
6. Taking into consideration the nature of allegations, I am of the view that custodial interrogation of the petitioners is not necessary.
However, the petitioners must subject themselves to interrogation.

Accordingly, this application is allowed on the following conditions:
(a) Petitioners shall appear before the Investigating Officer on 16.06.2025 and shall subject themselves to interrogation.

(b) If after interrogation, the Investigating Officer proposes to arrest the petitioners, then, they shall be released on bail on them executing a bond for Rs.50,000/- (Rupees fifty thousand only) each with two solvent sureties each for the like sum before the Investigating Officer.
(c) Petitioners shall appear before the Investigating Officer as and when required and shall also co-operate with the investigation.
(d) Petitioners shall not intimidate or attempt to influence the witnesses; nor shall they tamper with the evidence.
(e) Petitioners shall not commit any similar offences while they are on bail.
